extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal departments, military commanders, and state executives (e.g., governors)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of executive orders, military authorizations, and the President's annual message setting out policy recommendations, administrative instructions, and legal/organizational standards for federal, military, and civil administration during the 1861 insurrection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command communications routing
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications intended for the commanding general will hereafter be addressed direct to the adjutant-general. The duplicate returns, orders, and other papers heretofore sent to the assistant adjutant-general, headquarters of the army, will be discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headquarters of the army will be established in the city of Washington; this establishes a single channel (adjutant-general) for communications and discontinues prior duplicate submission to assistant adjutant-general.

rubrics_metrics.name: State militia to conform to Army Regulations and Articles of War
rubrics_metrics.description: State militia ... to be embodied and to be held in the camp and in the field, drilled, disciplined, and governed according to the Army Regulations and subject to the Articles of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acting as an embodied military force cooperating with U.S. troops, the State militia should be brought into the Army's regulatory and disciplinary framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: State militia geographic deployment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The said State militia not to be ordered out of the State except for the immediate defense of the State of Missouri, but to co-operate with the troops in the service of the United States in military operations within the State or necessary to its defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the deployment of state militia outside state borders to cases of immediate defense; permits cooperation with U.S. troops for operations within or necessary to the state's defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command precedence for mixed forces
rubrics_metrics.description: When officers of the State militia act with officers in the service of the United States of the same grade the officers of the United States service shall command the combined force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes clear seniority: in mixed operations between state militia and U.S. forces, U.S. officers of equivalent grade take command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal provisioning and pay for embodied state militia
rubrics_metrics.description: The State militia to be armed, equipped, clothed, subsisted, transported, and paid by the United States during such time as they shall be actually engaged as an embodied military force in service in accordance with regulations of the United States Army or general orders as issued from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal support (equipment, pay, transport, etc.) applies only while the militia are actually embodied and serving under Army regulations and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on federally funded state staff positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the State law requires him to appoint ... an adjutant-general, a commissary-general, an inspector-general, a quartermaster-general, a paymaster-general, and a surgeon-general, each with the rank of colonel of cavalry, yet he proposes that the Government of the United States pay only the adjutant-general, the quartermaster-general, and inspector-general, their services being necessary in the relations which would exist between the State militia and the United States. ... three only shall be reported to the United States for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid burdening the Treasury, the federal government will fund only those state staff officers necessary for interaction with U.S. forces; other state-appointed staff remain state-funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on general and staff numbers and federal compensation alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The State militia shall be commanded by a single major-general and by such number of brigadier-generals as shall allow one for a brigade of not less than four regiments, and that no greater number of staff officers shall be appointed for regimental, brigade, and division duties than as provided for in the act of Congress of the 22d July, 1861; and that ... the compensation that they shall receive from the United States shall only be that which belongs to the rank given by said act of Congress to officers in the United States service performing the same duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets ceilings on senior officer numbers (one major-general, brigadiers proportional to brigades of ≥4 regiments), ties staff appointment limits and federal pay to the July 22, 1861 Act of Congress to ensure parity and limit federal expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regimental and company officer composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The field officers of a regiment in the State militia are one colonel, one lieutenant-colonel, and one major, and the company officers are a captain, a first lieutenant, and a second lieutenant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the authorized officer structure at regiment and company levels for state militia when in federal service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of disbursing officers and anti-fraud regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Such staff officers in the service of the United States as may be necessary to act as disbursing officers for the State militia shall be assigned by the War Department for that duty; or, if such cannot be spared from their present duty, he will appoint such persons disbursing officers for the State militia as the President of the United States may designate. Such regulations as may be required, in the judgment of the President, to insure regularity of returns and to protect the United States from any fraudulent practices shall be observed and obeyed by all in office in the State militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal assignment (or presidentially designated appointments) of disbursing officers plus required regulations to ensure proper accounting and protect against fraud in disbursement of U.S. funds to state militia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of requisitions and additional regulations for economy
rubrics_metrics.description: All requisitions upon the different officers of the United States under this agreement to be made in substance in the same mode for the Missouri State militia as similar requisitions are made for troops in the service of the United States; and the Secretary of War will cause any additional regulations that may be necessary to insure regularity and economy in carrying this agreement into effect to be adopted and communicated to the Governor of Missouri for the government of the Missouri State militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requisitions for state militia equipment and supplies must follow the same procedures used for U.S. troops; the Secretary of War will promulgate further regulations to ensure regularity and economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's stipulation tying state commission to U.S. department commander
rubrics_metrics.description: When he commissions a major-general of militia it shall be the same person at the time in command of the United States Department of the West; and in case the United States shall change such commander of the department, he (the governor) will revoke the State commission given to the person relieved and give one to the person substituted to the United States command of said department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures unity of command by requiring the state's militia major-general commission to mirror the current U.S. departmental commander, with revocation/renewal upon U.S. changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential presidential communications via press intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall further it to the extent of my ability, by opening to you--as I do now--fully the policy of the Government,--its present views and future intentions when formed, giving you permission to communicate them to Gilmore for Greeley; and in case you go to Europe I will give these things direct to Gilmore. But all this must be on the express and explicit understanding that the fact of these communications coming from me shall be absolutely confidential,--not to be disclosed by Greeley to his nearest friend, or any of his subordinates. He will be, in effect, my mouthpiece, but I must not be known to be the speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes confidential sharing of government policy through a trusted press intermediary, conditioned on strict non-disclosure of the President as source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to suspend habeas corpus and exercise martial law in a department
rubrics_metrics.description: As an insurrection exists in the United States, and is in arms in the State of Missouri, you are hereby authorized and empowered to suspend the writ of habeas corpus within the limits of the military division under your command, and to exercise martial law as you find it necessary in your discretion to secure the public safety and the authority of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants discretionary authority to a departmental commander to suspend habeas corpus and enforce martial law where insurrection exists, for public safety and preservation of federal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to adopt adequate public defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: I recommend that adequate and ample measures be adopted for maintaining the public defenses on every side. While under this general recommendation provision for defending our seacoast line readily occurs to the mind, I also in the same connection ask the attention of Congress to our great lakes and rivers. It is believed that some fortifications and depots of arms and munitions, with harbor and navigation improvements, all at well-selected points upon these, would be of great importance to the national defense and preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for investment in fortifications, arms depots, and harbor/navigation improvements for seacoasts, lakes, and rivers to strengthen national defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military railroad construction for strategic connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: I deem it of importance that the loyal regions of east Tennessee and western North Carolina should be connected with Kentucky and other faithful parts of the Union by rail-road. I therefore recommend, as a military measure, that Congress provide for the construction of such rail-road as speedily as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends building a railroad (with route options) to link loyal regions for military purposes; cooperation with Kentucky and prompt construction emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of commerce from piracy and recapture authority
rubrics_metrics.description: For the more effectual protection of our extensive and valuable commerce in the Eastern seas especially, it seems to me that it would also be advisable to authorize the commanders of sailing vessels to recapture any prizes which pirates may make of United States vessels and their cargoes, and the consular courts now established by law in Eastern countries to adjudicate the cases in the event that this should not be objected to by the local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes legal authority for vessel commanders to recapture prizes from pirates and use consular courts for adjudication where local authorities permit, to protect commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and diplomatic representation for Haiti and Liberia
rubrics_metrics.description: If any good reason exists why we should persevere longer in withholding our recognition of the independence and sovereignty of Haiti and Liberia, I am unable to discern it. ... I submit for your consideration the expediency of an appropriation for maintaining a charge d'affaires near each of those new States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends recognizing Haiti and Liberia and funding diplomatic representation (charge d'affaires), citing potential commercial advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy in disbursement and energetic administration of wartime finances
rubrics_metrics.description: This fact imposes peculiar obligations to economy in disbursement and energy in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given broad public subscription and limited means, the administration must exercise frugality and vigorous management of funds raised for wartime needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of militia on a uniform basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendation of the Secretary for an organization of the militia upon a uniform basis is a subject of vital importance to the future safety of the country, and is commended to the serious attention of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorses consideration by Congress of standardized militia organization to enhance national security and interoperability with regular forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase corps of cadets at Military Academy
rubrics_metrics.description: The large addition to the regular army, in connection with the defection that has so considerably diminished the number of its officers, gives peculiar importance to his recommendation for increasing the corps of cadets to the greatest capacity of the Military Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for expanding cadet intake to replenish officer ranks lost to defections and army expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and compensation for chaplains in hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: By mere omission, I presume, Congress has failed to provide chaplains for hospitals occupied by volunteers. ... I therefore recommend that they be compensated at the same rate as chaplains in the army. I further suggest that general provision be made for chaplains to serve at hospitals, as well as with regiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates statutory provision and equal compensation for hospital chaplains serving volunteers, and broader policy to provide chaplains both in hospitals and regiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval organization reform by additional grades
rubrics_metrics.description: I would invite special attention to the recommendation of the Secretary for a more perfect organization of the navy by introducing additional grades in the service. The present organization is defective and unsatisfactory, and the suggestions submitted by the department will, it is believed, if adopted, obviate the difficulties alluded to, promote harmony, and increase the efficiency of the navy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports restructuring navy grade system to address organizational defects, promote harmony, and increase efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court / circuit court system reform options
rubrics_metrics.description: Three modifications occur to me, either of which, I think, would be an improvement upon our present system. Let the Supreme Court be of convenient number in every event; then, first, let the whole country be divided into circuits of convenient size, the Supreme judges to serve in a number of them corresponding to their own number, and independent circuit judges be provided for all the rest; or, secondly, let the Supreme judges be relieved from circuit duties and circuit judges provided for all the circuits; or, thirdly, dispense with circuit courts altogether, leaving the judicial functions wholly to the district courts and an independent Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers three alternative structural reforms (redistribute circuits with independent judges; relieve Supreme judges of circuit duties and appoint circuit judges; or abolish circuit courts) to remedy impracticalities in the existing judicial system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and consolidation of statute laws for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: It seems to me very important that the statute laws should be made as plain and intelligible as possible, and be reduced to as small a compass as may consist with the fullness and precision of the will of the Legislature and the perspicuity of its language. ... I respectfully recommend to Congress to consider of the subject, and if my suggestion be approved to devise such plan as to their wisdom shall seem most proper for the attainment of the end proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends Congress undertake revision/rewrite of existing acts (some 5000 acts across many volumes) to produce a clearer, more compact statutory code to aid administration and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary military courts or measures for administering justice in insurgent areas
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no courts or officers to whom the citizens of other States may apply for the enforcement of their lawful claims against citizens of the insurgent States ... Under these circumstances I have been urgently solicited to establish, by military power, courts to administer summary justice in such cases. I have thus far declined to do it ... I refer the whole matter to Congress, with the hope that a plan maybe devised for the administration of justice in all such parts of the insurgent States and Territories ... this, however, not to be a permanent institution, but a temporary substitute, and to cease as soon as the ordinary courts can be reestablished in peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes Congress devise temporary judicial mechanisms (not permanent) for areas under federal control to handle claims and administer justice until civil courts can be reestablished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court of Claims finality of judgments (subject to law appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: I commend to your careful consideration whether this power of making judgments final may not properly be given to the court, reserving the right of appeal on questions of law to the Supreme Court, with such other provisions as experience may have shown to be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests granting the Court of Claims final judgment power (to expedite claims against government), while preserving Supreme Court appellate review on legal questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regaining original District of Columbia boundaries for defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The present insurrection shows, I think, that the extension of this District across the Potomac River at the time of establishing the capital here was eminently wise, and consequently that the relinquishment of that portion of it which lies within the State of Virginia was unwise and dangerous. I submit for your consideration the expediency of regaining that part of the District and the restoration of the original boundaries thereof through negotiations with the State of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends negotiating with Virginia to recover the portion of the District ceded earlier, on grounds of capital defense and prudence given current insurrection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and striking from pension rolls for disloyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior has directed a suspension of the payment of the pensions of such persons upon proof of their disloyalty. I recommend that Congress authorize that officer to cause the names of such persons to be stricken from the pension rolls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends statutory authorization to suspend payments and remove pensioners proven to be disloyal to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for an agricultural and statistical bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports exhibiting the condition of our agriculture, commerce, and manufactures would present a fund of information of great practical value to the country. ... I venture the opinion that an agricultural and statistical bureau might profitably be organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates creation of a bureau to compile annual reports on agriculture, commerce, and manufactures to inform policy and encourage national prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of confiscated property and provision for freed persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Under and by virtue of the act of Congress entitled 'An act to confiscate property used for insurrectionary purposes,' approved August 6, 1861, the legal claims of certain persons to the labor and service of certain other persons have become forfeited, and numbers of the latter thus liberated are already dependent on the United States, and must be provided for in some way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes the government's responsibility to care for persons liberated by confiscation statutes and suggests that authorities devise means of support and disposition for those freed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and penalties for slave-trade suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: The execution of the laws for the suppression of the African slave trade has been confided to the Department of the Interior. ... Five vessels being fitted out for the slave trade have been seized and condemned. ... one captain, taken with a cargo of Africans on board his vessel, has been convicted of the highest grade of offense under our laws, the punishment of which is death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports active enforcement (seizures and convictions) and underscores that severe penalties (including death) apply for highest-grade offenses under anti–slave-trade laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prize/detention settlements by appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: I invite your attention to the correspondence ... relative to the detention of the British ship Perthshire in June last ... I recommend that an appropriation be made to satisfy the reasonable demand of the owners of the vessel for her detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends congressional appropriation to settle claims arising from mistaken or wrongful detention of foreign vessels, to uphold justice and international law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investing certain surplus proceeds for future claims
rubrics_metrics.description: I repeat the recommendation ... in regard to the disposition of the surplus which will probably remain after satisfying the claims of American citizens against China ... If ... it should not be deemed advisable to carry that recommendation into effect, I would suggest that authority be given for investing the principal, or the proceeds of the surplus referred to, in good securities, with a view to the satisfaction of such other just claims of our citizens against China as are not unlikely to arise hereafter in the course of our extensive trade with that empire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes investing surplus proceeds in secure securities to provide a fund for future just claims by citizens in trade with China.
